data.description:
## Context
Binding persistence currently shares `binding_store.py` with lifecycle policy. Extraction is unsafe until byte layout, load rules, and ordered partial-state failure behavior have direct oracles.

## Outcome
Create `BindingRepository` as the sole owner of live, retired, rotation, and alert files. It retains the original dictionaries and exact serialization behavior; no facade cutover occurs in this task.

## Plan
1. Start with direct failing tests over legacy and unknown-field fixtures, unchanged-save behavior, and exact sorted/indented/trailing-newline bytes.
2. Implement path ownership, current corruption rules, open typed views over the original dictionaries, dirty gating, tempfile cleanup, and per-file `os.replace`.
3. Add fault cuts for tempfile creation, rotation replace, retired replace, live replace, and alert write. Preserve rotation-before-live order, the newest inline rotation floor, and current raise/swallow behavior.
4. Make no multi-file atomicity, journal, eager rewrite, deep-copy, or publication claim.

## Testing
Run the direct repository suite with real temporary files and injected filesystem cuts. Tests assert exact surviving bytes and exceptions, not implementation call counts alone.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] Legacy and unknown-field fixtures round-trip to byte-identical sorted/indented/newline JSON with no eager write.
- [ ] An unchanged unit of work performs no replacement.
- [ ] Every named filesystem fault leaves the documented old/new file combination and preserves current raise/swallow behavior.
- [ ] Rotation is attempted before live replacement, and rotation-save failure retains the newest inline floor for later convergence.
- [ ] Repository views retain the original dictionaries rather than detached deep copies.

## Out of scope
Facade delegation, lifecycle extraction, tickets publication, and recovery cutover remain in later RP-02 tasks.
data.title: RP-02 S1 T1 — Build the byte-preserving binding repository
